# 12-Week Upper Body Programme for Subacromial Impingement Recovery

## Client Profile & Constraints
Your client presents with a recent subacromial impingement diagnosis (4 months post-diagnosis) with physiotherapy clearance for pain-free range of motion only. No overhead loading means we avoid pressing movements, lat pulldowns, and pull-ups. Her climbing background suggests good grip strength and body awareness, which we'll leverage. The office work context indicates postural dysfunction is likely contributing—we'll address this throughout.

---

## Programme Overview

**Structure:** Three 4-week phases with progressive complexity and load
- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):** Movement restoration and scapular control
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):** Strength building in safe ranges with postural integration
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):** Load progression and climbing-specific preparation

**Training frequency:** 3 sessions per week (Monday/Wednesday/Friday pattern recommended)
**Session duration:** 45–55 minutes
**Key principles:** Pain-free movement only; scapular stability before load; postural correction; gradual range expansion

---

## PHASE 1: Movement Restoration & Scapular Control (Weeks 1–4)

### Goals
- Establish pain-free movement patterns
- Activate and strengthen scapular stabilisers (lower trapezius, serratus anterior)
- Correct postural dysfunction from office work
- Build proprioceptive awareness in the shoulder complex

### Session Structure (All 3 sessions follow this template)

**Warm-up (8 minutes)**
- 2 minutes easy rowing machine (light resistance, focus on scapular retraction)
- Arm circles: 10 forward, 10 backward (small range)
- Band pull-aparts: 15 reps with light resistance band
- Scapular wall slides: 12 reps (see exercise detail below)

**Main Work (35 minutes)**

#### Week 1–2 Sessions

**Exercise 1: Scapular Wall Slides**
- 3 sets × 12 reps
- Stand with back against wall, feet 6 inches away
- Arms in "W" position (elbows bent 90°, shoulders abducted 45°)
- Slide arms upward along wall, maintaining contact, until elbows reach shoulder height (NOT overhead)
- Pause 1 second at top, return slowly
- *Cue:* "Squeeze shoulder blades down and back as you slide up"
- *Modification:* If any pinching, reduce range to 75% height

**Exercise 2: Prone Shoulder Taps**
- 3 sets × 10 reps per side
- Lie prone on bench, chest supported, feet on floor
- Arms hanging vertically below shoulders, light dumbbells (1–2 kg)
- Lift one arm slightly forward (15 cm), tap bench, return
- Alternate sides in controlled manner
- *Purpose:* Activates lower trapezius and serratus anterior
- *Cue:* "Initiate movement from your shoulder blade, not your arm"

**Exercise 3: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press (Isometric)**
- 3 sets × 20 seconds per side
- Half-kneeling position (right knee down, left foot forward)
- Cable machine set to chest height, handle in both hands at sternum
- Press handle straight forward 6 inches, hold against rotation
- *Purpose:* Anti-rotation core work; scapular stability under light load
- *Load:* 5–8 kg (very light)

**Exercise 4: Prone Y-T-I Sequence**
- 2 sets × 8 reps each position (Y, then T, then I)
- Lie prone on incline bench (30° angle), feet anchored
- **Y position:** Arms overhead at 45° angle, thumbs up, lift to shoulder height
- **T position:** Arms out to sides (90° abduction), thumbs up, lift to shoulder height
- **I position:** Arms overhead (180°), thumbs up, lift to shoulder height
- *Load:* Bodyweight only or 0.5 kg dumbbells
- *Cue:* "Lead with your shoulder blades, not your hands"

**Exercise 5: Dead Bug (Scapular Stability)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps per side
- Lie supine, arms extended toward ceiling (shoulders 90° flexion), knees bent 90°
- Lower right arm overhead while extending left leg (opposite limbs)
- Return to start, alternate
- *Purpose:* Teaches scapular stability during limb movement
- *Cue:* "Keep your lower back flat; don't let your ribs flare"

**Cool-down (5 minutes)**
- Chest doorway stretch: 30 seconds per side
- Child's pose: 45 seconds
- Gentle neck rolls: 5 each direction

---

#### Week 3–4 Sessions

Repeat Week 1–2 structure but with these progressions:

**Exercise 1: Scapular Wall Slides** → Increase range to full shoulder height (still not overhead)

**Exercise 2: Prone Shoulder Taps** → Increase to 3 kg dumbbells; add 1-second pause at top

**Exercise 3: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press** → Increase to 10 kg; extend hold to 30 seconds

**Exercise 4: Prone Y-T-I Sequence** → Add 1 kg dumbbells; increase to 10 reps per position

**Exercise 5: Dead Bug** → Add 0.5 kg ankle weights; increase to 12 reps per side

**New Exercise 6: Prone Horizontal Abduction (Reverse Pec Deck)**
- 3 sets × 12 reps
- Sit at reverse pec deck machine, chest against pad
- Handles at shoulder height, arms bent 90°
- Pull handles outward in horizontal plane (scapular retraction)
- *Load:* 8–10 kg
- *Cue:* "Initiate with your shoulder blades; squeeze them together"

---

## PHASE 2: Strength Building & Postural Integration (Weeks 5–8)

### Goals
- Build strength in scapular stabilisers and posterior chain
- Introduce horizontal pressing in pain-free range
- Integrate postural correction into loaded movements
- Prepare for climbing-specific demands

### Session Structure

**Warm-up (8 minutes)** — Same as Phase 1

**Main Work (40 minutes)**

#### Week 5–6 Sessions

**Exercise 1: Prone Incline Dumbbell Press**
- 4 sets × 8–10 reps
- Lie prone on 45° incline bench, feet anchored
- Dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows bent 90°
- Press dumbbells forward (horizontal plane, NOT upward)
- Lower with control
- *Load:* 6–8 kg per hand (start conservative)
- *Purpose:* Horizontal pressing without overhead component; scapular stability under load
- *Cue:* "Press forward, not up. Keep your shoulder blades stable."

**Exercise 2: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row (Supported)**
- 4 sets × 10 reps per side
- Half-kneeling position, one knee down
- Dumbbell in opposite hand, arm hanging
- Row dumbbell to hip, elbow tracking close to body
- *Load:* 8–10 kg
- *Purpose:* Unilateral pulling; anti-rotation core engagement
- *Cue:* "Initiate with your shoulder blade; don't just pull with your arm"

**Exercise 3: Reverse Pec Deck**
- 3 sets × 12 reps
- *Load:* 12–15 kg (increased from Phase 1)

**Exercise 4: Prone Y-T-I Sequence**
- 2 sets × 10 reps each position
- *Load:* 1.5 kg dumbbells

**Exercise 5: Pallof Press (Dynamic)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps per side
- Half-kneeling position
- Cable at chest height
- Press handle forward, return to chest, repeat
- *Load:* 12–15 kg
- *Cue:* "Resist rotation; stay square"

**Exercise 6: Prone Shoulder Taps**
- 3 sets × 12 reps per side
- *Load:* 3 kg dumbbells

**Exercise 7: Scapular Push-Up (Wall or Incline)**
- 3 sets × 8 reps
- Hands on wall or incline bench, arms straight
- Retract scapulae (shoulder blades down and back), creating small movement
- Protract scapulae (shoulder blades forward), returning to start
- *Purpose:* Scapular control in weight-bearing position
- *Cue:* "This is a tiny movement—just your shoulder blades moving"

---

#### Week 7–8 Sessions

Repeat Week 5–6 structure with these progressions:

**Exercise 1: Prone Incline Dumbbell Press** → 8–12 kg per hand; increase to 4 sets × 10–12 reps

**Exercise 2: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row** → 10–12 kg; add 1-second pause at top

**Exercise 3: Reverse Pec Deck** → 15–18 kg

**Exercise 4: Prone Y-T-I Sequence** → 2 kg dumbbells; 12 reps per position

**Exercise 5: Pallof Press** → 15–18 kg; increase to 12 reps per side

**Exercise 6: Prone Shoulder Taps** → 4 kg dumbbells

**Exercise 7: Scapular Push-Up** → Progress to incline bench (lower angle); 10 reps

**New Exercise 8: Inverted Row (Assisted or Incline)**
- 3 sets × 8–10 reps
- Set barbell in rack at waist height (or use TRX)
- Lie underneath, grip shoulder-width, heels on ground
- Pull chest toward bar, lower with control
- *Load:* Adjust height to make 8–10 reps challenging
- *Purpose:* Horizontal pulling; scapular retraction under load
- *Cue:* "Pull your chest to the bar; squeeze your shoulder blades"

---

## PHASE 3: Load Progression & Climbing Preparation (Weeks 9–12)

### Goals
- Build strength and muscular endurance for climbing demands
- Progress to more challenging pulling patterns (still horizontal)
- Introduce climbing-specific movements
- Establish sustainable maintenance programme

### Session Structure

**Warm-up (8 minutes)** — Same as previous phases

**Main Work (45 minutes)**

#### Week 9–10 Sessions

**Exercise 1: Prone Incline Dumbbell Press**
- 4 sets × 10–12 reps
- *Load:* 10–14 kg per hand

**Exercise 2: Inverted Row (Incline)**
- 4 sets × 10–12 reps
- *Load:* Adjust height so last 2 reps are challenging

**Exercise 3: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row**
- 4 sets × 10–12 reps per side
- *Load:* 12–14 kg

**Exercise 4: Reverse Pec Deck**
- 3 sets × 12–15 reps
- *Load:* 18–22 kg

**Exercise 5: Pallof Press (Dynamic)**
- 3 sets × 12 reps per side
- *Load:* 18–20 kg

**Exercise 6: Prone Y-T-I Sequence**
- 2 sets × 12 reps each position
- *Load:* 2 kg dumbbells

**Exercise 7: Scapular Push-Up (Incline)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps
- Progress to lower incline angle

**Exercise 8: Farmer's Carry (Offset)**
- 3 sets × 30 meters per side
- Hold dumbbell in one hand, walk
- *Load:* 12–16 kg
- *Purpose:* Unilateral grip strength; anti-lateral flexion core work
- *Cue:* "Stay upright; don't lean toward the weight"

**New Exercise 9: Horizontal Band Pull-Apart (Resistance Band)**
- 3 sets × 15 reps
- Hold band at chest height, arms straight
- Pull band apart, stretching across chest
- *Load:* Medium resistance band
- *Purpose:* Scapular retraction endurance; postural correction
- *Cue:* "Lead with your shoulder blades"

---

#### Week 11–12 Sessions

Repeat Week 9–10 structure with these progressions:

**Exercise 1: Prone Incline Dumbbell Press** → 12–16 kg per hand; 4 sets × 12 reps

**Exercise 2: Inverted Row** → Lower incline angle; 4 sets × 12–15 reps

**Exercise 3: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row** → 14–16 kg; 4 sets × 12 reps per side

**Exercise 4: Reverse Pec Deck** → 22–25 kg; 3 sets × 15 reps

**Exercise 5: Pallof Press** → 20–25 kg; 3 sets × 12–15 reps per side

**Exercise 6: Prone Y-T-I Sequence** → 2.5 kg dumbbells; 12 reps per position

**Exercise 7: Scapular Push-Up** → Progress to floor (full weight-bearing); 3 sets × 12 reps

**Exercise 8: Farmer's Carry** → 16–20 kg; 3 sets × 40 meters per side

**Exercise 9: Horizontal Band Pull-Apart** → Heavy resistance band; 3 sets × 20 reps

**New Exercise 10: Climbing-Specific Pulling (Assisted Chin-Up or Horizontal Pulling Variation)**
- 3 sets × 6–8 reps
- **Option A:** Assisted chin-up machine (if shoulder feels stable) — pull with elbows driving down and back
- **Option B:** Horizontal pulling with rope attachment (cable row) — 12–15 kg, 8–10 reps
- *Purpose:* Prepare for climbing demands; test shoulder readiness
- *Cue:* "If any pinching sensation, stop immediately and revert to horizontal rows"

---

## Nutrition & Recovery Recommendations

### Nutrition
- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g per kg bodyweight daily (supports muscle repair and adaptation)
- **Timing:** Consume 20–30 g protein within 2 hours post-workout
- **Anti-inflammatory foods:** Fatty fish (omega-3s), berries, leafy greens, turmeric (supports shoulder recovery)
- **Hydration:** 2.5–3 litres daily, more on training days

### Recovery
- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours nightly (critical for tissue repair and adaptation)
- **Between-session mobility:** On non-training days, perform 10-minute shoulder mobility routine:
  - Sleeper stretch: 30 seconds per side
  - Cross-body shoulder stretch: 30 seconds per side
  - Thoracic rotations: 10 per side
  - Band pull-aparts: 15 reps
- **Foam rolling:** Upper back and thoracic spine, 60 seconds per area, 3–4 times weekly
- **Ice/heat:** If any mild inflammation post-session, ice for 10 minutes; otherwise, heat for relaxation

### Monitoring & Progression Rules
- **Pain rule:** Any sharp or pinching pain = stop exercise immediately; regress to previous week's load
- **RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion):** Final 2 reps of each set should feel challenging but controlled (RPE 7–8/10)
- **Weekly check-in:** Ask client about pain levels, range of motion, and climbing readiness
- **Progression gates:** Only advance load if all reps are pain-free and form is pristine

---

## Climbing Return Protocol (Weeks 11–12 Onwards)

By Week 11–12, if the client is pain-free and demonstrates strong scapular control:

- **Week 11:** Light bouldering (V0–V1 grade) on vertical walls only, 2 sessions per week, 20 minutes max
- **Week 12:** Progress to V1–V2, introduce slight overhangs (< 10°), 2 sessions per week, 30 minutes max
- **Post-Week 12:** Gradual return to normal climbing, monitoring for any recurrence of symptoms

**Climbing-specific gym work to maintain:**
- Continue Exercises 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 from Phase 3 indefinitely (maintenance programme)
- Reduce frequency to 2 sessions per week once climbing resumes
- Prioritise scapular stability work before climbing sessions

---

## Summary Table: Exercise Progression

| Exercise | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 |
|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| Scapular Wall Slides | 3×12 (BW) | Removed | Removed |
| Prone Shoulder Taps | 3×10 (1–2 kg) | 3×12 (3–4 kg) | Removed |
| Pallof Press | 3×20s iso (5–8 kg) | 3×10 dyn (12–15 kg) | 3×12–15 (20–25 kg) |
| Prone Y-T-I | 2×8 (BW–0.5 kg) | 2×10 (1–1.5 kg) | 2×12 (2–2.5 kg) |
| Dead Bug | 3×10 (BW) | Removed | Removed |
| Reverse Pec Deck | 3×12 (8–10 kg) | 3×12 (12–18 kg) | 3×15 (22–25 kg) |
| Prone Incline Press | — | 4×8–10 (6–8 kg) | 4×12 (12–16 kg) |
| Single-Arm Row | — | 4×10 (8–10 kg) | 4×12 (14–16 kg) |
| Scapular Push-Up | — | 3×8 (wall/incline) | 3×12 (floor) |
| Inverted Row | — | 3×8–10 (incline) | 4×12–15 (lower angle) |
| Pallof Press Dynamic | — | 3×10 (12–15 kg) | 3×12–15 (20–25 kg) |
| Farmer's Carry | — | 3×30m (12–16 kg) | 3×40m (16–20 kg) |
| Band Pull-Apart | — | — | 3×15–20 (medium–heavy) |
| Climbing-Specific Pull | — | — | 3×6–8 (assisted/horizontal) |

---

## Key Coaching Cues Throughout Programme

1. **"Shoulder blades first"** — Always initiate movement from scapular muscles, not arm muscles
2. **"Pain-free range only"** — Stop immediately if any pinching or sharp sensation
3. **"Postural integrity"** — Maintain neutral spine and upright posture in all exercises
4. **"Slow and controlled"** — Eccentric (lowering) phase should be 2–3 seconds
5. **"Squeeze at the top"** — Pause 1 second at end-range to maximise scapular activation

---

## Final Notes

This programme is conservative by design. Your client's subacromial impingement is recent, and the physio's clearance for pain-free range only must be respected. The progression is gradual and contingent on pain-free movement. If at any point she experiences symptoms, regress immediately and consider a physio check-in.

Her climbing background is an asset—she likely has good body awareness and will understand cues about scapular control. Use this to your advantage, and frame the programme as "building the foundation for stronger, pain-free climbing."

By Week 12, if all goes well, she should have significantly improved scapular stability, postural control, and readiness to return to climbing with a sustainable maintenance programme in place.
